channel.title: The Indicator from Planet Money
channel.description:
A bite-sized show about big ideas. From the people who make Planet Money, The Indicator helps you make sense of what's happening in today's economy. It's a quick hit of insight into money, work, and business. Monday through Friday, in 10 minutes or less.
Sign up for our newsletter.

Support public media by joining NPR+ at plus.npr.org. You’ll get perks for over 25 NPR podcasts, including bonus episodes for Planet Money and sponsor-free listening for The Indicator.

item.title: Will AI take my job? Ask an economist!
item.description:
Are AI job losses showing up in the job numbers? What does a pro-worker approach to AI development look like? What advice do you have for college students? It’s our latest “Ask an Economist” segment, where listeners get to pose questions directly to economists about hot topics in the news. 

Daron Acemoglu, a Nobel Prize-winning professor at MIT, and Erik Brynjolfsson, a professor at Stanford and director of the Stanford Digital Economy Lab, joined us to weigh in on AI and the future of work. 

To listen to the whole hour-long conversation or join us for our next “Ask an Economist,” make sure you’re signed up for NPR+ at plus.npr.org. 

Fact checking by  Cooper Katz McKim.

item.title: How crypto world made inroads in Pakistan
item.description:
Pakistan in recent years has taken a U-turn on cryptocurrency, opting to regulate digital assets instead of outright banning them. On today’s show, what the country’s crypto boosters hope to gain for their efforts and why religious scholars are still skeptical of its value. 

Fact checking by Leyla Doss.
